newsitem.title: USA: Compaq CEO sees $40 bln annual revs by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Compaq CEO sees $40 bln annual revs by 2000.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp President and Chief Executive Officer Eckhard Pfeiffer on Tuesday said he expected the company to have annual revenues of $40 billion before the end of the century.

Pfeiffer said the figure was based on a recent review of the Houston-based company's financial prospects. "We clearly have the opportunity to be a $40 billion company before the end of the decade," he told reporters after a ceremony marking the sale of Compaq's one millionth server.
Compaq had $14.8 billion in revenues in 1995. Pfeiffer said the expected revenue increase would come from sales growth and new products.

When asked if he agreed with projections that the market for personal computers would grow close to 20 percent in 1997, Pfeiffer said "that's about what we anticipate...I think we are seeing a very strong commercial environment."
"Next year in a broad sense I believe the Intranet and Internet phenomena is going to be the driver (of the market)," Pfeiffer said.

Pfeiffer said sales in the fourth quarter were showing "a seasonal uptick." "Consumer and commercial (sales) have their peak in the fourth quarter and that is going to be the case again in 1996," he said. "There's a seasonal uptick -- it's more pronounced on the consumer side but it's really strong across the board."
Pfeiffer said sales of Compaq's new handheld computer, which was put on the market two days ago, have been stronger than expected.
"Response to the product is very strong. We had planned a certain volume and we're scrambling to pick up the volume because demand is stronger than anticipated," he said.
